 Distribution System Supervisor Colin Young will present on updates and additions to Electric Service Regulations (Multiple small changes to wording throughout the document). He will then submit for board approval RESOLUTION 2294-24 Establishing the Current Electric Service Regulations and Requirements and Rescinding Resolution 2248-22. 

 Addition: Section 3.12 Developer Substation Capacity Charge – Calculation added to ensure single large land developments contribute to substation capacity increases. 

 Addition: Section 1 Customer Funds definition – Clarifying language for customer money. 

 Addition: Section 8.A.8 Paid Estimate Updates – Creates a mechanism for passing cost increases on to customers with projects last more than 1 year. 

 Addition: Section 8.A.9 Return of Customer Funds – Creates a limit on how long customer funds will be held by the District.

matters.body: Regular BOC Meeting PUD No. 1 of Clallam County at 1:30 PM
matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 May 12, 2025 - Regular BOC Meeting PUD No. 1 of Clallam County at 1:30 PM 
 Category 
 4. Business Items 
 Subject 
 A. Recommendation Memo 250804 to Solicit Bids for Diamond Point Road Overground to Underground Distribution 
 Type 
 Action (Vote to approve or authorize) 
 Recommended Action 
 Approve Recommendation Memo 250804 to Solicit Bids for Diamond Point Road Overground to Underground Distribution 

 Engineer Timothy Christman will submit for Board approval Recommendation Memo 250804 to authorize the solicitation of bids to prequalified contractors for the construction of distribution along Diamond Point Road in 
 of distribution along Diamond Point Road in Sequim, WA. Installation of (1) switch cabinet and vault, which will require the ability to move and set equipment up to 10,000 lbs. Installation of (1) open-delta padmount transformer bank vault, (2) riser pole assemblies on existing poles. Excavation of 6,000 feet of trench with depth at 42", installation of 18,000 of conduit, installation of 22,000 feet of underground conductor, and installation of (6) splice and junction vaults. 
 This project is expected to be partially funded through Washington State Department of Commerce – Grid Resilience Program, funded with federal monies through the U.S. Department of Energy, IIJA Section 40101(d) Grid Resilience State and Tribal Formula Grant. These funds assist the District in addressing the critical need to upgrade overhead powerlines to underground services in areas vulnerable and prone to frequent outages due to severe weather, natural disasters, and potential wildfires. The engineer’s estimate for the project is $540,000. 
 Staff requests a motion, second, and vote to authorize District staff to publish a notice in the Seattle Daily Journal of Commerce and by such other means as determined by staff to be prudent, inviting sealed proposals from prequalified contractors. 

 §
